roadmap.goal: Let a Portfolio's Dependency Field name a Jira link phrase or an Azure DevOps relation end, reading dependencies from it and saying on Refresh History when the name matched nothing or points both ways; then let a Work Tracking Connection carry defaults for the Teams' and Portfolios' Parent Override Field, the Dependency, Size Estimate and Feature Owner Fields and the Estimation bundle, which every owner follows unless it keeps its own value, with one log entry per default-changing save naming the followers, a pre-save dialog that counts them, and an update queued for exactly the owners whose fetch moved.
roadmap.source: docs/feature/epic-6303-configure-once-per-connection/feature-delta.md (DISCUSS to DISTILL, including the maintainer UI decisions and the DISTILL wave decisions with the pinned names), slices/slice-01..12 (07 dropped), distill/red-classification.md, design/maintainer-decisions-2026-10-16.md, docs/product/architecture/adr-241 (inherited setting), adr-242 (connection save), adr-243 (dependency link), adr-244 (refresh findings), brief.md epic-6303 section
roadmap.paradigm: OOP backend (.NET 10, ports and adapters; NUnit 4.6 + Moq + WebApplicationFactory over real EF, SQLite file and a Postgres container for the upgrade test); React 18 + TypeScript frontend (Vitest + RTL); Playwright with POMs for the one walking skeleton. No Hypothesis/PBT mandate: it is a Python pilot and this corpus has declined it on the record (story 6301). Where DESIGN says 'property-based test' (the movers rule, the effective-value rule, the Estimation bundle), write an exhaustive TestCase / TestCaseSource table over the whole small domain instead; no new test dependency.
standing_constraints: Before every step, read docs/ci-learnings.md and pre-apply every rule it lists (CLAUDE.md requires it); the backend and frontend preflights below are its current extract, the ledger wins where they differ.

Comments are rare and why-only, written for a stranger. No code comment may cite an internal reference (D10, DDD-4, AC-F.1, G-R1, CA-8, U-13, slice ids, ADR-241..244). Say the reason in plain language or write nothing. The one exception is a narrow #pragma warning disable, which carries its reason inline; an ADO item number is fine there. The renamed own-value property mapped to an old column name carries a one-line why. Fix offending comments in any file you touch.

Un-skip discipline. A step removes [Ignore(PendingEpic6303.SliceNN)] (or Ignore = PendingEpic6303.SliceNN on an upgrade TestCase row) only from the tests it lists, and only once they pass. Frontend tests are plain it.skip in EditConnection.defaults.test.tsx, AdvancedInputs.connectionDefault.test.tsx and RefreshHistorySection.findings.test.tsx (no slice marker in the call; the @us tag decides: US-01..03 slices 01..03, US-04 slice 05a, US-05 slice 06, US-11 slice 12); the E2E is test.fixme in ConnectionDefaults.spec.ts. If a listed test already passes before the step's production change, prove it can fail by sabotage-by-substitution (keep every parameter read, assign the dependency to a discard; never comment a call out, never if(false), never a bare block), restore, then un-skip. At the end of each slice, grep -rn 'PendingEpic6303.SliceNN' Lighthouse.Backend returns nothing for that slice, delete that constant from PendingEpic6303.cs, and the it.skip tests for that slice's user story are gone. Active guards (green today) are listed per step and must stay green.

SCAFFOLD inventory: grep -rn SCAFFOLD Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend Lighthouse.Frontend/src lists exactly one line at hand-off, Services/Interfaces/IConnectionSaveService.cs:3. Step 05-03 implements and registers the service and removes that marker; the handle and outcome records may be reshaped as long as the race scenario's decorator in ConnectionDefaultsAcceptanceTest follows. models/SystemInfo/RefreshLog.ts already carries the RefreshFinding types DISTILL scaffolded, without a marker; step 01-05 makes them real. After slice 05a the grep is empty.

Copy is pinned by the maintainer (UI-1..UI-6) and by the tests; use it verbatim, through Terminology for configurable words only: section region 'Defaults for Teams and Portfolios' with groups 'Teams' and 'Portfolios' and the lead 'Teams and Portfolios on this connection use these unless they set their own.'; owner entry 'Connection default (<value>)' with helper 'Set on the <tracker> connection.'; could-not-load 'Could not load this connection.' with Try again; dialog titles 'Update N Teams and M Portfolios?' and 'Change the Estimation default?'; Refresh History 'The Dependency Field names "<named>", and no <Feature> carries that link. Links seen: <seen>.', 'The Dependency Field names "<named>", which points both ways. Name one end: "<a>" or "<b>".', 'The Parent Override Field points at an Azure DevOps relation type, which only the Dependency Field reads.' and the label 'as of the full download on 16 Oct, 09:12'; refusal '"Caused by" cannot be removed. It is the Teams' Parent Override Field default, and Ledger uses it as its own. Nothing was saved.'; the log entry 'Connection "Jira DC – Payments" changed the Teams' Parent Override Field default from "Caused by" to "Parent Link"; 3 Teams follow it: Fraud Signals, Ops Tooling, Mobile Wallet; 3 updates queued.' (followers in creation order; 'no Team follows it' when none). Tracker values stay literal. A phrase repeated three times in one file lives in one const (S1192).

Names pinned by the tests (rename only consistently across tests and code): refresh-log rows latestFullRunFindings [{kind, setting, named, seen[]}] and latestFullRunAt; kinds NamedLinkMatchedNothing, NamedLinkPointsBothWays, RelationTypeHasNoDirection, RelationTypeNamedWithoutItsEnd, RelationTypeNotYetReadForDependencies (slice 03 only), RelationTypeCannotBeReadHere; settings ParentOverrideField, DependencyField, SizeEstimateField, FeatureOwnerField, EstimationField. Owner DTO: the existing id member carries the effective value, beside it <member>Source (ConnectionDefault / Own, strings out, strings or ints in) and <member>DefaultName, plus workTrackingSystem. Connection DTO: one nested defaults member with parentOverrideForTeams, estimationForTeams, parentOverrideForPortfolios, dependencyFieldForPortfolios, sizeEstimateFieldForPortfolios, featureOwnerFieldForPortfolios, estimationForPortfolios; supportedDefaults; usedBy.followers keyed by the same names. Source columns ParentOverrideSource (Teams and Portfolios), DependencyFieldSource, SizeEstimateFieldSource, FeatureOwnerFieldSource, EstimationSource; 0 = follows, 1 = own.

Local gates before every step's commit, each read in full (never piped through tail or head): (1) dotnet build in Lighthouse.Backend, zero warnings other than NU1901-NU1904 (NU1903 on SignalR.Common in the test project predates this Epic); (2) the analyzer sweep, dotnet format analyzers Lighthouse.sln --severity info --verify-no-changes --no-restore, logged and filtered to this change's files with BOTH halves, { git diff --name-only <slice base>; git status --porcelain -uall | awk '{print $2}'; } | grep '\.cs$', run before every push and not only before the commit; (3) dotnet test --filter "TestCategory!=Integration&TestCategory!=JiraIntegration&TestCategory!=LinearIntegration&TestCategory!=AdoIntegration&TestCategory!=ServiceNowIntegration" (the upgrade test needs Docker for its Postgres container and runs in this filter); (4) for frontend steps pnpm test, then pnpm build with zero errors and warnings (prebuild runs biome check --write; remove any */docs symlinks first); (5) before an E2E-touching commit, the affected Playwright spec run locally. Never run dotnet test --no-build while another build is writing bin/. A red suite spanning unrelated subsystems is a concurrent build, not a regression.

Backend preflight, pre-applied in every new or edited line: CA1859 concrete types on non-public returns, parameters and locals (List<T>, Dictionary<K,V>, never IReadOnlyList or an interface; a test helper returns the concrete subject); CA1861 constant arrays in tests hoisted to private static readonly; NUnit2045 independent asserts in using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope()), inside helpers too; NUnit2056 never Assert.Multiple; NUnit2046 Has.Count / Has.Length; NUnit4002 Is.Zero and Is.Default; NUnit1028 TestCaseSource providers private static, then re-check CA1859; CA1869 the findings JsonSerializerOptions is one static readonly field (production and tests); CA1806 capture every Try* result; S6964 every new value-type member on a [FromBody] DTO (sources, the defaults bundle flags) is nullable; S107 WorkTrackingSystemConnectionController stays at 7 (IConnectionSaveService replaces IDomainEventDispatcher), ConnectionSaveService takes at most 5, WorkItemService already carries a narrow S107 pragma and gains no parameter; S4136 overloads adjacent; S125 no prose comment line ends in ';'; S2325/S4487 stubs read instance state (instance-derived NotImplementedException message); S3267 LINQ over accumulating foreach; S3776 keep Commit, the findings step, the apply rule and the dialog's open condition under 15 (a lambda counts toward its method); S3236 no explicit parameter names to ThrowIf* guards; S1192 shared copy in one const; S6618 string.Create(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture, ...) never FormattableString.Invariant; CS8524 a discard-free switch over SettingSource or the finding kind carries a narrow #pragma warning disable CS8524 with its reason inline; a mock asserted with Times.Never is built in [SetUp]; System.Text.Json outside a controller sets PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true.

Frontend preflight: S6754 every useState destructured as [thing, setThing]; S7761 data-* only through dataset; S7735 no negated condition in a ternary; S3358 no ternary inside a template-literal slot on a ternary branch, no inline pluralisation ternaries in template literals (extract a helper); S7764 globalThis over window; S7770 pass single-arg pure functions directly; readonly props on every JSX-returning function; a catch parameter is named error_; zod .nullable() for every backend T? member, never bare .optional() (the refresh-log findings stay optional because older backends omit them); SettingSource mirrored as the string-literal union 'ConnectionDefault' | 'Own' (enums serialise as strings out). Before changing a visible label, accessible name or data-testid, grep -rn the old text in Lighthouse.EndToEndTests/ in the same edit (the owner dropdowns gain a first entry; the Parent Override InputLabel gains a labelId).

Widening a shared contract: before editing WorkTrackingSystemOptionsOwner, Portfolio, IWorkItemQueryOwner, WorkTrackingSystemConnection, WorkItemBase/Feature, SyncOutcome, RefreshLog, the settings DTOs (SettingsOwnerDtoBase, PortfolioSettingDto), WorkTrackingSystemConnectionDto or IWorkTrackingSystemConnectionUsage, grep the short AND the fully qualified name in production and test projects (test doubles and builders are where the forgotten writer lives: WorkItemServiceTestBuilder, the Team/Portfolio test builders, DemoDataFactory) and extend the builders first. Every writer of an owner setting goes through follow() / own(value) once the setters are private; DemoDataFactory's demo Teams keep their Estimation through own(value) so every demo-data E2E reads what it reads today. RefreshLog is serialised directly: grep the tests for any payload-shape list that must gain the findings members.

EF migrations (01-03, 05-02, 08-01, 09-01, 10-01, 11-01, 12-01): dotnet restore && dotnet build over the whole solution from Lighthouse.Backend first (migration DLLs are HintPath references), port 5432 free, then pwsh Lighthouse.Backend/Create-Migration.ps1 -MigrationName <Name> - never dotnet ef migrations add. Expand-only. Source columns are int not null with defaultValue: 0 on BOTH providers (an older build's inserts rely on the database default), no CLR initializer; default columns nullable; the RefreshLog findings column nullable text. Hand-add the two data steps to BOTH providers' generated files, in this order: (a) clear the owner's value where NOT EXISTS an AdditionalFieldDefinition with that id AND the owner's own WorkTrackingSystemConnectionId (a field of another connection counts as dangling; for Estimation a dangling field empties the whole bundle in each provider's stored form); (b) set the source to 1 where the value is still not null. Postgres identifiers double-quoted. The renamed own-value property maps to the existing column name, so no column change may appear for it. Then the ordered second pass (dotnet build each migrations csproj --no-incremental, then the solution --no-incremental) and a throwaway Database__Provider=sqlite start with the Kestrel keys overridden (never 5169), grepping its output for PendingModelChanges. The InMemory provider never warns. Every new column on Teams, Portfolios and WorkTrackingSystemConnections also goes into Lighthouse.Backend.Tests/TestHelpers/HistoricalSchemaPatch.cs (both migration fixtures seed all three tables), or unrelated migration fixtures go red naming the column; RefreshLog is not seeded there, so it needs no entry.

Architecture tests: the new rules (WorkTrackingSystemConnectionController depends on neither IDomainEventDispatcher nor FetchFingerprint, matched by type; the effective-value, movers, in-use, apply rules and the supported-defaults map depend on nothing outside Models and the BCL, following the StalenessPolicyPurityArchUnitTest precedent; Services does not depend on API.DTO; the ADO connector holds no field of the relation-type listing's type) are verified with dotnet build -c Release && dotnet test -c Release --filter FullyQualifiedName~Architecture, because CI builds Release and Debug lies. Never assert an ArchUnit edge that exists only inside an async method body. New Models files do not start with WorkTrackingSystemConnection (that prefix is on the CI shared-path whitelist); only the connection model itself carries it.

Test-time budget: a new backend test class stays under 34 s and a frontend test file under 63 s in CI (Scripts/test-timings/test-time-budget.json; warn-only until the switch). Watch ConnectionDefaultsUpgradeMigrationTests (Postgres container) and the Slice05b class (22 cases). Speed up before allowlisting.

Live connectors: the default filtered run excludes them. Run deliberately, once per slice, never in a loop: JiraIntegration in slices 01 and 02 (at least JiraDependencyDogfoodTest, JiraLinkTypeDogfoodTest and the class extended for the named link type); AdoIntegration in slices 03 and 04 (AzureDevOpsWorkTrackingConnectorTest Validate and relations paths, plus the slice 03 spike against the dev organisation). Never LinearIntegration or ServiceNowIntegration locally (the Linear key is shared with CI). CI wakes every live suite on 05-03 (Program.cs) and on every step that edits Models/WorkTrackingSystemConnection.cs (05a, 08..12); triage a red there before the push counts as judged: a 4xx/429 from Linear, ServiceNow or GitHub is environmental, a Jira or ADO dependency/parent failure is this Epic's; a 429-only red is re-run once, and if still red the slice brief records that Sonar did not judge it and a green judged run lands before the next slice is pushed. Never print a token value.

Work in the main checkout /storage/repos/Lighthouse with absolute paths. Each Story finishes before the next starts (#6300 slices 01-02, #6312 03-04, #6304 05a-06, #6313 08-12); no step of a later Story starts before the earlier Story's last step is green.

Commits: focused conventional commits per step through des-commit with the step id; scopes dependencies for slices 01-04 and connection-defaults for 05a-12 (feat(...), test(...), refactor(...)); refactors in their own commit, before the behaviour commit, under the same step id when a step carries both. Push only when green and when the maintainer releases the hold. Mutation testing is NOT in this roadmap: Stryker runs once after DELIVER on frozen code (DEVOPS scope), which is why every rule the acceptance tests exercise also gets unit tests here. Docs prose (docs/portfolios/edit.md, docs/teams/edit.md, docs/settings/worktrackingsystems.md, docs/settings/systeminfo.md, docs/concepts/worktrackingsystems/jira.md and azuredevops.md, docs/features/features.md, docs/concepts/howlighthouseforecasts.md), @screenshots, release notes (crediting Steve Pereira, plus the per-slice repaired-value sentence and the follow-clears-own-value item), website follow-ups and ADO tags are finalize work, not roadmap steps. Two exceptions stay in their steps because the house rule ties them to the change: ARCHITECTURE.md (§3, §5, §16 rows for ADR-241..244) and the one sentence DEVOPS owes docs/settings/usagedata.md row :62 in slice 06.
Usage data: no new event (DEVOPS: a connection default is configuration, not usage). Do not append to UsageDataEventName; the only usagedata.md change is the slice-06 sentence above.

Mutation testing owner and timing: the AFK orchestrator runs /mutation-testing once, after the whole-feature refactor and adversarial review, on frozen code, >= 80% kill rate per stack (Stryker.NET excluding the acceptance suite; Stryker for the frontend files this Epic touched).
deviations: Walking-skeleton placement: in phases 02, 05, 07 and 12 the @walking_skeleton scenario is not on the phase's first step, by design. 02-01/02-02 build the backend half that 02-03, the first step a user sees, reads. 05-01..05-03 are the refactor, the migration and the service the skeleton runs through, so 05-04 is the first step that can carry a slice scenario through the driving port; 05-08, the connection page's Defaults section, is the frontend skeleton DISTILL pinned and needs the DTO from 05-04. 07-01 is the backend skeleton; 07-03, the save dialog, is the frontend one and needs the follower counts 07-02 adds. 12-01 is the migration; 12-02 is the backend skeleton, and 12-05 is the one Playwright skeleton, which needs every earlier step. Each skeleton sits on the first step that can make it pass and is never deferred past it.
Frontend tests carry no slice marker; their @us tag decides the step (US-01..03 slices 01..03, US-04 slice 05a, US-05 slice 06, US-11 slice 12).

Tags such as @us-02 or @us-05b in files outside this Epic's three frontend test files (ReportView, Reports panels, EditConnection.fieldChange, refinement tests) belong to other features' DISTILL waves and are not this Epic's scenarios.

phases.name: Slice 01 — A Jira Portfolio reads dependencies from the link phrase it names
phases.description: US-01, Story #6300. The Dependency Field may resolve to a Jira link type; the typed phrase sets the end; DependencySourceSelector gains a third source; a type name or a shared phrase reads nothing and raises one NamedLinkPointsBothWays finding on Refresh History. Because DISTILL pins that finding in this slice, the findings path DESIGN placed in slice 02 (RefreshFinding, evidence on the Feature, the WorkItemService step, SyncOutcome, the RefreshLog column and its migration, the refresh-log read, the frontend rendering) lands here; slice 02 adds the nothing-matched kind and the latest-full-run read. Not #6300's release point. Brief: slices/slice-01-6300-jira-dependencies-from-a-named-link-phrase.md.

steps.name: Walking skeleton: a Feature waits on what its named one-way link points at
criteria: A Portfolio whose Dependency Field names the Additional Field whose reference is 'depends on' shows, through GET /api/latest/features/references after its refresh, PAY-112 waiting on PAY-98 and PAY-98 waiting on nothing
The stored references say DependencySource.TrackerLink; no enum member is added
The Jira request count of a refresh naming the link equals the count of the same refresh naming nothing
steps.implementation_notes: ~2h. Thinnest line through every layer: the reference resolution the connector already does for Parent Override (field first, then link type by name or phrase, JiraWorkTrackingConnector.cs ~:1993-2019, :2058-2070; IssueExtensions.cs ~:106-120, :190-212) now also serves the Dependency Field; where today a link-type Dependency Field stores an empty value (~:1733), the connector collects, per Feature, the counterpart key on the end the typed phrase reads as (JiraIssueLinkType.DirectionReadFrom), reusing the walker ResolveParentFromLinks uses, and hands it to DependencySourceSelector's new third source ('a link type the Portfolio named'); the selector decides, as it does for the tracker link and the field. Only the one-direction happy path here; the other end, case and rename, and the both-ways refusal are 01-02 and 01-03. issuelinks already arrives with *all, so no request is added; if one ever seems needed it goes through JiraRestRoutes with its Data Center answer. Re-read the Jira connector line numbers with fresh=true before citing them. LOCAL GATE: wire-fixture unit cases in the existing IssueExtensions tests over TrackerWireFormats for this path.

steps.name: The named end sets the direction, in any case and under a renamed phrase, and replaces is blocked by; a field stays a field
criteria: Naming 'is depended on by' shows PAY-98 waiting on PAY-112
A renamed inward phrase typed in another case ('Waits For') reads like the stock phrase: PAY-140 waits on PAY-77, PAY-77 on nothing
A Portfolio naming a link reads only that link; its is blocked by links no longer count for it
A real field whose name equals a link phrase, an ordinary field, and no Dependency Field all read exactly as before
steps.implementation_notes: ~1.5h. Exhaustive TestCase table on DependencySourceSelector (pure): {no field, ordinary field, named link} x {Linear/CSV opt-out, Jira, ADO} -> which source and which references; the named-link source replaces the tracker link (one link type, no union). Wire-fixture unit cases for both ends, rename, case-insensitive match on name, inward and outward phrase. ARCHITECTURE.md §3 in the same change: the Dependency Field may name a link type (a third dependency source), and correct the sentence saying the connector declares the parent source (that port was never built).

steps.name: A name that points both ways reads nothing and is recorded as one finding on the Portfolio's refresh row
steps.scenario_name: WorkItemServiceTest findings cases (new, DISTILL left them to DELIVER): one NamedLinkPointsBothWays finding per whole-query Portfolio fetch however many Features carry it; none on a delta fetch; RefreshLogTest round trip of the findings column
criteria: A Portfolio fetch whose Dependency Field resolved to a type name or a phrase both ends share records no dependency and returns exactly one finding of kind NamedLinkPointsBothWays, setting DependencyField, naming what was typed and listing both phrases as seen
A delta fetch writes no finding; a Team fetch writes none
The finding reaches the Portfolio's RefreshLog row and reads back unchanged, and the log carries one aggregated Warning line for it
A refresh log row written before this change, with the column null, still reads
steps.implementation_notes: ~2.5h, tagged for sizing review and kept whole on purpose: the findings path is one chain (record -> service -> SyncOutcome -> RefreshLog) and each half is untestable without the other; split at the migration if it runs long. Follows ADR-244 and the story-6301 path: the connector puts a transient, [NotMapped] value on each Feature it returns (what the Dependency Field resolved to, the phrases seen), carried by the copy constructor; WorkItemService decides once per fetch in a private step beside PlaceWhatTheLinksLeftOpen in ResolveRemoteFeatureFetch (~:984 after the 6247 merge; re-read fresh), whole-query branch only, at most one finding per kind, one aggregated log line; SyncOutcome gains an init member; RefreshLog gains one nullable text column (System.Text.Json with a static readonly options field, CA1869), appended last; PortfolioUpdater copies it beside RecordsPlacedFromLinksNamingMoreThanOneParent (~:167). The kind is a closed enum serialised by name in the column. EF migration per the standing constraint: Create-Migration.ps1 -MigrationName AddRefreshFindingsToRefreshLog (DEVOPS listed this migration under slice 02; it moves here). No HistoricalSchemaPatch entry (RefreshLog is not seeded there). WorkItemService gains no constructor parameter. Re-read WorkItemService.cs, WorkItemServiceTest.cs and WorkItemServiceTestBuilder.cs with fresh=true first: story 6247 changed all three.

steps.name: Refresh History's read sends the Portfolio's findings, and the both-ways scenarios pass end to end
criteria: GET /api/latest/systeminfo/refreshlog carries latestFullRunFindings and latestFullRunAt on every row of the Portfolio, the same on each row, with exactly one NamedLinkPointsBothWays finding naming 'Dependency' and seeing 'depends on' and 'is depended on by'
No Feature of the Portfolio waits on anything after that refresh
An entity whose rows carry no findings is sent without the members' content changing what older clients read
steps.implementation_notes: ~1h. The read (SystemInfoController GetRefreshLog ~:95) attaches, per entity, the findings of its latest row that has them and that row's time; the backend picks the row, the browser never searches. Taking only Mode == Full rows is slice 02's scenario (02-02) and lands there, so this step reads the latest whole-query row the findings step wrote. Grep the tests for any refresh-log payload-shape list that must gain the two members. SLICE-END: none yet; slice 01 ends at 01-05.

steps.name: Refresh History shows a both-ways finding under the Portfolio's figures, and stays as it was without one
steps.scenario_name: a link type named by its name rather than one end asks which end is meant
criteria: Selecting the Portfolio shows 'The Dependency Field names "Blocks", which points both ways. Name one end: "blocks" or "is blocked by".' under its figures
Rows without the findings members keep rendering their history (the slice-02 guards stay skipped until 02-03)
steps.implementation_notes: ~1h. Render from the existing read; no new fetch, so the section's existing spinner and alert are its loading and could-not-load looks. Sentences built in the browser from kind + setting + named + seen, configurable words through Terminology, tracker values literal; a kind the browser does not know renders nothing (rows written by a build that knew RelationTypeNotYetReadForDependencies will outlive slice 04). Copy as module constants pinned against literals. SLICE-END GATES: grep -rn 'PendingEpic6303.Slice01' Lighthouse.Backend is empty and the Slice01 constant is deleted; JiraIntegration run deliberately once (standing constraint); dogfood AC-1.7 / OUT-6303-dependencies-recovered on the dev instance (O-P1 baseline counted BEFORE this slice's first push; P2 link on a handful of Features) and record both numbers in the slice brief's Changed assumptions.

phases.name: Slice 02 — A named Jira link that matched nothing says so on Refresh History
phases.description: US-02, Story #6300's release point. The connector's 'none of your links is called …' check no longer returns early for a link-type Dependency Field and becomes NamedLinkMatchedNothing evidence; Refresh History shows the latest FULL run's findings with that run's time, so a cheap refresh never blanks them. Brief: slices/slice-02-6300-a-named-link-that-matched-nothing-says-so.md.

steps.name: Nothing matched the named link: one finding per whole-query refresh listing the links seen, silent otherwise
criteria: A Portfolio naming 'depends on' whose Features carry only other links gets one NamedLinkMatchedNothing finding listing the phrases seen, and one log line, however many Features it has
Anything matching, no links at all, or an ordinary field: Refresh History sends an empty findings list, not an absent one
A Portfolio naming nothing keeps today's is blocked by diagnostic in the log
steps.implementation_notes: ~2h. Generalise ReportLinksThatMeantNothingHere (JiraWorkTrackingConnector.cs ~:1275-1309): the expected name is the named phrase when a link type is named, is blocked by otherwise; lift the early return at ~:1282 for a link-type field only. The decision moves to the 01-03 findings step (evidence on the records), whole-query only, silent when anything matched or nothing is linked. Several scenarios assert an empty list rather than null: a full run that found nothing writes an empty list, so the read sends []. If the connector-side check becomes its own small class, it enters the mutation scope (DEVOPS).

steps.name: A cheap refresh keeps showing the full download's finding and its time until the next full download
criteria: After a full run with a finding and then a delta run, every row of the Portfolio carries the full run's findings and the full run's time
A later full run without the finding clears it
A full run older than the window the section shows still counts
steps.implementation_notes: ~1h. The read takes, per entity, the latest row with Mode == SyncMode.Full, whatever window is asked for. SLICE-PREP: JiraIntegration run deliberately once; dogfood on slice 01's Portfolio deliberately mis-named ('depend on'), read the finding, correct, re-run; record in the slice brief.

steps.name: Refresh History says which named link nothing carries, which links were seen, and as of which full download
steps.scenario_name: a named link nothing carries is shown with the links that were seen and when that was found; active guards a full download that found nothing to say shows no finding and no label, rows from a backend that sends no findings still show their history
criteria: With Feature renamed to Epic, the section shows 'The Dependency Field names "depends on", and no Epic carries that link. Links seen: is blocked by, relates to.'
Beside it, 'as of the full download on 16 Oct, 09:12', formatted as a local day and time
An empty findings list shows no finding and no label; rows from a backend that sends no findings still render the history
steps.implementation_notes: ~45 min. Format the time through the existing local-date utilities (src/utils/date/localDate.ts), never toISOString; the suites run in Europe/Zurich. SLICE-END GATES: grep -rn 'PendingEpic6303.Slice02' Lighthouse.Backend empty, constant deleted, no US-01/US-02 it.skip left. #6300 is releasable.

phases.name: Slice 03 — An Azure DevOps relation type is accepted where a field name goes
phases.description: US-03 validate half, Story #6312. A reference that misses the field list is looked up once per call in the organisation's relation types (never remembered on the cached connector); Validate accepts reference name plus end, refuses a typo listing the types, and says so when the listing is refused; a refresh no longer reports it as a missing field; until slice 04 a relation-type Dependency Field reads nothing and says not yet; in any other setting it reads as nothing named and says why. Brief: slices/slice-03-6312-ado-relation-type-accepted-as-a-reference.md.

steps.name: Spike, then Validate accepts a relation type reference with its end, in any case, asking at most once
criteria: POST /api/latest/worktrackingsystemconnections/validate answers 200 for an Additional Field referencing 'Contoso.DependsOn-Forward', also typed in another case
Validate lists the organisation's relation types at most once per call, and not at all when every reference is a field
A field whose name collides with a relation type validates as the field
steps.implementation_notes: ~2.5h including the spike. SPIKE FIRST (DISTILL pre-requisite 1, P8, OQ-1): with a vso.work PAT, record a real GET _apis/wit/workitemrelationtypes answer from the dev organisation (SDK GetRelationTypesAsync is the candidate), replace the provisional AnAzureDevOpsOrganisation.AsListed with it, and add a Server 2022 fixture if one can be obtained (otherwise say so in the brief). Record which directional types the organisation lists: slice 04's vehicle is chosen from them. IF THE LISTING IS REFUSED with vso.work: stop and report to the maintainer before building on it (the slice's learning hypothesis). Then: the listing is a value created at the start of one Validate call for that call's connection and passed down that call's chain; the connector holds no field of its type (ArchUnit or reflection check).
